questions.q: Why do 14 January Receivables transactions fail to generate accounting?
options: The transactions were entered with an invalid customer
Account 7850 (Freight Out) was never added to the Subledger Accounting Account Rule for that transaction type
The transactions exceeded a dollar threshold requiring manual approval
The Receivables period was already closed
questions.explain: Account 7850 was added to the chart of accounts in December, but the SLA Account Rule for the freight-charge transaction type was never updated, so Create Accounting can't find an applicable rule.

questions.q: What accounting status and total dollar amount result from this SLA gap?
options: Status: Posted; $0.00 impact
Status: Incomplete; $4,250.00 total, not posted to GL
Status: Error; $18,400.00 total
Status: Incomplete; $27,750.00 total
questions.explain: The 14 affected transactions total $4,250.00 and remain in Incomplete accounting status, unposted to the General Ledger.

questions.q: What is journal INTERCO-JAN-0131, and what is its status at month-end?
options: A $27,750.00 intercompany overhead allocation journal, left in Draft/Unposted status
A $4,250.00 freight correction journal, fully posted
A $18,400.00 AP accrual reversal, rejected by validation
A $9,200.00 bank adjustment journal, pending approval
questions.explain: Victor Okafor prepares and saves INTERCO-JAN-0131 for $27,750.00, intending a final review, but it is never submitted for posting and stays in Draft status.

questions.q: How many total problems does Chapter 2 end up planting across the whole chapter, according to this lesson's recap?
options: Three
Four
Six
Eight
questions.explain: The recap lists six problems total: the GRNI accrual, the AR misapplication, the miscategorized asset, the bank variance, the Incomplete SLA transactions, and the unposted intercompany journal.

questions.q: What common thread does this lesson draw across all six planted problems?
options: They were all caused by the same single employee
They are all individually explainable and easy to miss alone, but collectively disrupt the month-end close
They all involve the same dollar amount
They all originate in the Canadian subsidiary's ledger
questions.explain: The lesson explicitly notes that each problem is individually small and explainable, but together they are why the close doesn't go smoothly.
